$comment: One table of control calls and the sentence each must fail with when its OPC UA session dies before the server answers. Driven through BOTH runtimes: tests/unit/test_retry_policy.py and packages/server-node/test/retry-policy.test.mjs read this file and assert the same string. The same pattern as argument-validation.json, and for the same reason — two hand-written copies of a rule are two rules. The wording itself comes from contract/tools.json -> errors.uncertainOutcome; what is pinned here is the `targets` substitution, which each runtime builds from the tool's own `guard` and which is the part a human reads to decide what to check before sending the call again. Values are never in it: a setpoint is process data, and this message goes to the same stream the audit trail does.

cases.name: a single-node write names the node it was aimed at
a batch write names every node, so none of them is assumed to have landed
a method call names the object and the method, which is what authorised it
an acknowledgement names the condition, not the comment
